title: Gasoline demand to the minerals under the FCC catalyst
why: The crack spread is the visible end. The load path runs through the refinery's fluid catalytic cracking unit, into the catalyst, into the zeolite, into the rare earths that stabilise it, and out to a small set of separation plants. Almost none of that is in any cross-asset model.
greatest_assumption: Rare earth and molybdenum demand from refining catalysts is material enough at the margin to move the mineral markets before the refining margin moves them.
kill_test: Refinery catalyst demand is flat or shrinking (catalyst life extensions, lower gasoline runs) while mineral prices move for unrelated reasons.

kill_test: Transformer output rises with flat GOES supply, or GOES capacity additions do not change lead times.

title: Gas turbine to the superalloys and their byproducts
why: Turbine slots gate new gas capacity. The slots are gated by castings, and the castings are gated by a set of metals most people cannot name: rhenium, hafnium, cobalt, and the nickel that goes into every blade.
greatest_assumption: Single-crystal blade casting capacity, not assembly capacity, is the limiting step in turbine deliveries.
kill_test: Turbine output rises while blade casting capacity is flat, or casting expansion does not shorten slots.

title: HVDC to the valves, the cables and the ships

greatest_assumption: Family level compute price changes lead provider capex and power commitments rather than merely reflecting demand that is already visible elsewhere.

edges.condition: Shortage invites capital.
edges.falsifier: Capital arrives without scarcity.

edges.condition: Capex clusters because competitors can see the same shortage.
edges.falsifier: Builds are staggered enough to match demand.

edges.condition: Price collapse bankrupts the levered.
edges.falsifier: Declines are shallow enough to avoid failures.

edges.condition: Distressed assets need operators with cheap capital.
edges.falsifier: Assets stay stranded.

edges.condition: Turbine scarcity in 1999 to 2002 is the same marker as the current cycle.
edges.falsifier: Current turbine scarcity has a different cause.

edges.condition: Dark fiber is the same overbuild object as idle interconnection capacity.
edges.falsifier: Interconnection capacity is consumed on arrival.

edges.condition: Hyperscale self-build is the same capital pattern as the current build.
edges.falsifier: Capital is all equity and preleased.

title: Entry windows: the edge must work without latency, and then latency adds
why: A fast estimate of what a filing or disclosure means is worth size and timing, not existence. Every chain here must survive at zero latency advantage, and the entry windows are written down so the improvement can be measured.
greatest_assumption: The edge is profitable with no latency advantage, so speed improves size and price rather than being the reason the edge exists.
kill_test: The strategy's profit disappears when entries are delayed by one bar, which would prove it was a latency business.

nodes.name: Event timestamp
nodes.meaning: the moment a filing, queue update or disclosure becomes public

nodes.name: Interpretation latency
nodes.meaning: the seconds to minutes needed to read and classify a disclosure

nodes.name: State estimation job
nodes.meaning: a fast estimate of the state that the disclosure updates, including spectral and quantum sampling methods as candidates
nodes.source: docs/inbox notes on QGM and spectral methods

nodes.name: Entry window
nodes.meaning: the time during which a position can be established before the information is fully in prices

nodes.name: Capacity and slippage
nodes.meaning: the size that can be entered before impact consumes the edge

nodes.name: Edge decay half life
nodes.meaning: how long the signal pays after the event

nodes.name: Zero latency rehearsal
nodes.meaning: the mandatory run where entries are delayed to prove the edge does not need speed

edges.condition: The clock starts at publication.
edges.falsifier: Timestamps are unavailable or wrong.

edges.condition: The parser hands a classified event to the estimator.
edges.falsifier: The estimate needs no classification.

edges.condition: A faster estimate reaches the entry window earlier.
edges.falsifier: The window is long enough that speed does not matter.

edges.condition: The window length bounds the size that can be filled.
edges.falsifier: Liquidity exceeds what the window allows.

edges.condition: Impact consumed at entry competes with the decay of the edge.
edges.falsifier: Impact is negligible at target size.

edges.condition: Delayed entries test whether the edge exists without speed.
edges.falsifier: Delayed entry performs the same, which is fine, and the rehearsal still decides.

title: Compute rentals to provider revenue to equity, written as nodes
why: The provider family claims rental change reaches provider economics through revenue. The aggregate was tested and came back inside the null (T19), and the family level signs disagree, which leaves the middle object open: which rental family each provider actually sells, and what its revenue is levered to.
greatest_assumption: Provider revenue is levered to level variables, revenue per megawatt and contracted share, once family price mapping is removed, and filings are enough to measure them.
kill_test: After the exposure map is written, family specific transmission shows no association for any provider family pair.

nodes.name: Provider revenue line
nodes.meaning: the quarterly revenue of a listed provider, taken from SEC XBRL
observables: SEC XBRL revenue concepts, quarterly durations

nodes.name: Rental to revenue link
nodes.meaning: the transmission from rental price change into provider revenue growth

nodes.name: Provider to family exposure map
nodes.meaning: which rental family each provider actually sells, and the share of revenue exposed to it
nodes.source: own study, T21: falsified raw and relative; strongest association on the provider the map excludes

nodes.name: Revenue per contracted megawatt
nodes.meaning: the revenue a provider earns per megawatt of committed capacity, the bridge between power and rental economics
nodes.source: own study, T21: the level object that replaces family price mapping

nodes.name: Contracted against merchant share
nodes.meaning: the share of capacity committed under long contracts versus sold at market

nodes.name: Lease and renewal spread
nodes.meaning: the change in pricing on renewed or newly signed capacity

nodes.name: Power cost pass through
nodes.meaning: the clause that passes electricity cost to the tenant or leaves it with the provider

nodes.name: Depreciation policy on accelerator fleets
nodes.meaning: the useful life assumption applied to GPUs and related equipment, and its effect on reported earnings

nodes.name: Tenant concentration
nodes.meaning: the share of revenue from the largest tenants

nodes.name: Financing cost and structure
nodes.meaning: the debt and securitisation structures funding the capacity, and the cost of that funding

nodes.name: Equity transmission
nodes.meaning: the listed expression of provider economics: cash flow revision to multiple to price

nodes.name: Capex intensity against revenue
nodes.meaning: quarterly capex divided by quarterly revenue, the input side measured against the revenue it serves
observables: SEC XBRL capex and revenue concepts
nodes.source: own study, T23: MSFT 0.471 last against 0.136 mean, ORCL 2.017 against 0.212

edges.condition: Rental resets pass into provider revenue with a lag.
edges.falsifier: Rental changes leave revenue growth unmoved in the same direction, as the aggregate test found (T19).

edges.condition: Each provider's revenue is levered to specific families, so family level tests replace the aggregate.
edges.falsifier: No provider family pair shows any association once the map is used.

edges.condition: Transmission shows up per unit of committed capacity before it shows up in total revenue.
edges.falsifier: Revenue per megawatt moves against total revenue for the same provider.

edges.condition: Contracted share sets how much of the rental change reaches revenue inside the year.
edges.falsifier: Revenue per megawatt is insensitive to the contracted share.

edges.condition: Renewal pricing is the observed version of the rental change at the provider level.
edges.falsifier: Lease spreads move opposite to rental prices for the same period.

edges.condition: Where power cost passes through, rental economics reach the provider undiluted by energy cost.
edges.falsifier: Provider margin per megawatt is flat across pass through and non pass through contracts.

edges.condition: Concentrated tenants hold pricing power and slow the pass through of rental resets.
edges.falsifier: Revenue growth is unrelated to tenant concentration.

edges.condition: Useful life assumptions convert cash economics into reported earnings.
edges.falsifier: Earnings revisions are insensitive to depreciation policy changes.

edges.condition: Funding cost sets the discount applied to capacity cash flows.
edges.falsifier: Equity reaction to capacity news is unrelated to funding structure.

edges.condition: Revenue per megawatt is the cash flow line that equity prices.
edges.falsifier: Equity revisions follow total revenue while revenue per megawatt stays flat.

edges.condition: Securitised and debt funded capacity shows up as contracted revenue before it shows up as equity value.
edges.falsifier: Funded capacity adds no contracted revenue.

edges.condition: With family price mapping retired, the transmission object is the level variable: revenue per contracted megawatt.
edges.falsifier: Revenue per megawatt is fixed by signed contracts across the whole window and carries no rental information.

edges.condition: Investment outruns revenue before it either lifts revenue or compresses margin.
edges.falsifier: Capex intensity is flat across the panel, as META and EQIX show.

edges.condition: High intensity becomes depreciation and interest inside reported earnings.
edges.falsifier: Earnings absorb intensity without any change in useful life or leverage.

title: The forced seller, written as nodes, and the cost hurdle it faces
why: The cascade family claims a forced seller creates a dislocation that reverts enough to pay for entry after the flow. The reversion was measured on the recorded tape (T20): the percentile levels do not clear the cost hurdle, and the frozen conjunction's gross does, on six events. The nodes here write the mechanism and the constraint, so the next pass tests identity and cheaper entry rather than wider ladders.
greatest_assumption: The forced seller is identifiable and the unfilled events are the reversion, so entry is taken immediately and maker orders serve size rather than edge.
kill_test: Extended tape shows the conjunction's gross reversion inside the cost hurdle at the same horizons.

nodes.name: Trigger identity
nodes.meaning: who is forced: the account whose engine must sell, not the price move that follows

nodes.name: Liquidation engine
nodes.meaning: the margin engine that converts a price move into a market order, and its triggers

nodes.name: Funding extreme
nodes.meaning: funding beyond its trailing distribution, the cost of holding the crowded side

nodes.name: Open interest collapse
nodes.meaning: the fall in open interest that identifies closing rather than new positioning
nodes.source: recorded tape; part of the frozen conjunction

nodes.name: Depth vacuum
nodes.meaning: book depth inside ten basis points below its trailing percentile, the room to move price

nodes.name: Dislocation magnitude
nodes.meaning: the size of the move at the condition, in basis points and in trailing sigmas
observables: one minute and five minute moves
nodes.source: recorded tape; 103 events at the top one percent

nodes.name: Reversion half life
nodes.meaning: how much of the dislocation returns by one, five and fifteen minutes, gross and net

nodes.name: Cost hurdle
nodes.meaning: the round trip cost of taking the reversion: taker fee plus spread, near ten basis points at base and twenty when doubled

nodes.name: Maker entry candidate
nodes.meaning: resting at the dislocation extreme instead of taking the reversion, to cut the hurdle
observables: best bid and ask from the tape
nodes.source: own study, T22: fills 33 to 47 percent, paired +4.6 to +17.3 bps, absolute net at or below zero

nodes.name: Capacity by depth
nodes.meaning: the notional the reversion can carry, bounded by the depth present at the event
observables: median depth at events: about 1.9 million dollars at the top one percent level, 950 dollars when the book is thin

nodes.name: Market heterogeneity
nodes.meaning: the same level reverts in one market and not another: SPX +14.7 basis points gross against GAS -4.0 at fifteen minutes

nodes.name: Zero latency entry rule
nodes.meaning: enter at the close of the condition bar, after the flow, so speed improves the fill and is never the reason the edge exists

nodes.name: Fill selection
nodes.meaning: which events fill a resting order, and whether the fills are the adverse ones
observables: resting order fills against recorded book
nodes.source: own study, T22: at the frozen conjunction the two fills are the events that kept moving

edges.condition: An identifiable forced account is what makes the engine act.
edges.falsifier: Dislocations of the same size occur with no identifiable forced side.

edges.condition: Forced liquidation closes positions, so open interest falls with the move.
edges.falsifier: Large moves at the same conditions occur with rising open interest.

edges.condition: Closing flow consumes the resting book and leaves thinner depth behind it.
edges.falsifier: Depth at the events is no thinner than its trailing level.

edges.condition: Extreme funding marks the crowded side that breaks first.
edges.falsifier: Funding extremes precede no larger moves than average, as the measured level suggests (taken direction was wrong).

edges.condition: The larger the forced move, the more room to revert.
edges.falsifier: Reversion shows no relation to move size.

edges.condition: Only reversion above the round trip cost is capitalizable.
edges.falsifier: Net reversion is positive where gross is below the hurdle.

edges.condition: A resting order replaces the taker fee and half the spread with fill risk.
edges.falsifier: Maker fills at the extreme do not improve the realized net.

edges.condition: Maker entry is only possible where the book has size to fill.
edges.falsifier: Fills appear at events whose depth is too thin to matter.

edges.condition: Reversion pools only markets whose structure supports it.
edges.falsifier: The per market differences vanish with more events.

edges.condition: The measured reversion is the one available at bar close, with no speed used.
edges.falsifier: The reversion exists only inside the first seconds after the event.

edges.condition: A resting order fills precisely when the market keeps going, so the fill set is not the event set.
edges.falsifier: Filled events and unfilled events show the same forward reversion.

edges.condition: The reversion lives in the events that do not come back to a resting price.
edges.falsifier: Unfilled events are the ones that continue.
